draft.title: Comparing data sets
card: To compare two data sets, look at the same measures for both: a typical value (mean or median) and the spread (range or IQR).
Graphs help. Two box plots drawn on the same scale show the medians, spreads and ranges side by side.
Write the comparison in words and use the numbers. Example: Team A has a median of 40 and Team B has 32, so Team A usually scores higher.
A smaller spread means more consistent results. A fair conclusion uses both a typical value and the spread, and it is stated in the context of the data.
draft.remember: Compare the typical value and the spread, using the same measures for both sets.

a.q: Team A scores have a median of 40 and an IQR of 6. Team B scores have a median of 32 and an IQR of 12. Which is true?
opts: Team A usually scores higher and is more consistent
Team B usually scores higher and is more consistent
Team A usually scores higher and is less consistent
Team B usually scores lower and is more consistent
a.why: Team A has the higher median, so it usually scores higher. Its IQR is smaller, so its scores are more consistent. A larger IQR does not mean better scores, it means more spread.
a.clue: Compare the medians for typical scores, then the IQRs for consistency.

b.q: Mia's café sells a median of 52 coffees a day with a range of 20. Sam's café sells a median of 52 with a range of 50. What is a fair conclusion?
opts: Typical sales are equal, but Sam's sales vary more
Mia's café sells more coffees than Sam's
Sam's café sells more coffees than Mia's
Both cafés have the same spread of sales
b.why: The medians are equal, so typical daily sales are the same. Sam's range of 50 is larger than Mia's 20, so his sales vary more. A larger range does not mean higher sales.
b.clue: Check the medians first, then compare the ranges.

a.best: Team A usually scores higher and is more consistent

b.best: Typical sales are equal, but Sam's sales vary more

problems.detail: The right option is clearly the longest (about 50 characters against about 40) and the only one with two clauses covering both typical value and spread, so a student could pick it on its shape without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The facts and answers are correct. In question b, the right option stands out as the longest and the only two-part statement, so it could be guessed without knowing the idea.
